positive_limbs: Incurred in gaining or producing your assessable income, OR
Necessarily incurred in carrying on a business for that purpose
negative_limbs: Capital or of a capital nature (deduct under Div 40/43 instead)
Incurred in gaining exempt or non-assessable non-exempt income
general_test.apportionment_rule: Where an expense serves both an income-producing and a private purpose it must be apportioned on a fair and reasonable basis. Claiming 100% of a mixed-purpose expense is the single most common audit trigger.

categories.label: D1
categories.name: Work-related car expenses

methods.evidence: reasonable basis for the kilometre estimate (diary, roster, client list)
12-week continuous logbook valid for 5 years + odometer readings + all running cost receipts

deductible_when: Travel between two separate workplaces or employers
Travel from your workplace to an alternative workplace (client site) and back
Carrying bulky tools where there is no secure storage at the workplace
Your home is a genuine base of employment and you travel to a workplace
never_deductible: Ordinary home-to-work commuting, even if you work outside normal hours
Travel where the employer provides a car or reimburses on a cents-per-km basis
Travel made private by a detour (school drop-off, shopping) - apportion it out
categories.risk_note: The ATO data-matches registration and toll records. A claim at exactly 5,000 km with no supporting basis is a standard review flag.

categories.label: D2
categories.name: Work-related travel expenses
deductible_when: Travel undertaken in performing your work duties, away from home overnight
Accommodation, meals and incidentals while travelling for work
never_deductible: Living-away-from-home costs (that is an FBT matter, not a deduction)
Costs of a spouse or family member accompanying you
The private portion of a trip that mixes work and holiday - apportion strictly
categories.substantiation: Written evidence for all costs; a travel diary is required for trips of 6 or more consecutive nights away from home.

categories.label: D3
categories.name: Work-related clothing, laundry and dry cleaning
deductible_when: Occupation-specific clothing that distinctly identifies your profession (chef's checks, barrister's robes)
Protective clothing and footwear (steel caps, hi-vis, non-slip nursing shoes, sun protection for outdoor work)
A compulsory uniform that is distinctive to the employer, enforced by a strictly applied policy
A registered non-compulsory uniform (must be on the Register of Approved Occupational Clothing)
never_deductible: Conventional clothing, however unwillingly worn - a plain suit, black pants, white shirt
Everyday footwear, even where the employer specifies a colour
Gym wear for fitness instructors unless it carries a compulsory logo
categories.risk_note: Laundry claims under $150 need no receipts but still need a reasonable basis. This is the most commonly over-claimed label.

categories.label: D4
categories.name: Work-related self-education expenses
deductible_when: The course maintains or improves a skill or specific knowledge required in your CURRENT employment
The course is likely to result in increased income from your current employment
never_deductible: Education to obtain NEW employment or open a new income-earning activity
HELP/HECS-HELP loan repayments (s 26-20 expressly denies these)
Courses undertaken while not employed in the relevant field
deductible_items: travel to and from the place of education
depreciation on a computer used for study

subcategories.name: Working from home

methods.record: total actual hours worked from home for the full year - contemporaneous record required
receipts plus a reasonable basis for the work-related percentage of each cost

never_deductible: Rent, mortgage interest, rates or home insurance for an employee - occupancy costs require a dedicated place of business and can cost you the main residence CGT exemption
Coffee, tea, milk and other general household items
Costs your employer reimbursed
subcategories.cgt_warning: Claiming occupancy costs can partially forfeit the main residence CGT exemption under s 118-190. Flag to an adviser before doing this.

subcategories.name: Tools and equipment
subcategories.rule: Immediate deduction if cost is $300 or less and the item is not part of a set; otherwise depreciate under Div 40.

subcategories.name: Phone and internet
subcategories.rule: Work-use percentage only, established by a representative 4-week record. Cannot be claimed separately if using the fixed-rate WFH method.

subcategories.name: Union fees and professional association subscriptions
subcategories.rule: Fully deductible where membership relates to current employment.

subcategories.name: Income protection insurance
subcategories.rule: Deductible only for the portion covering loss of INCOME. Premiums for life, trauma or TPD cover are not deductible, nor are policies held inside super.

subcategories.name: Professional journals and industry subscriptions
subcategories.rule: Deductible where directly connected to earning income.

categories.label: D6
categories.name: Low-value pool deduction
categories.rule: Assets costing under $1,000, or written down to under $1,000, may be pooled and depreciated at 18.75% in the first year and 37.5% thereafter.

categories.label: D7
categories.name: Interest and dividend deductions
deductible_when: Interest on money borrowed to acquire income-producing investments
Ongoing management and advice fees relating to existing investments
Investment journal subscriptions
never_deductible: Initial investment advice fees for setting up a new portfolio (capital)
Interest on a loan used for private purposes, even if secured against an investment

categories.label: D9
categories.name: Gifts or donations
deductible_when: Gift of $2 or more to an endorsed Deductible Gift Recipient (DGR)
never_deductible: Raffle tickets, chocolates, badges and anything where you received a material benefit
Crowdfunding for an individual
School building fund contributions that are actually fees
Gifts to a non-DGR, however worthy
categories.check: Verify DGR endorsement on the ABN Lookup register before claiming.
categories.risk_note: A deduction cannot create or increase a tax loss for individuals; excess may be spread over up to 5 years by election.

categories.label: D10
categories.name: Cost of managing tax affairs
deductible_when: Registered tax agent fees
Tax reference material
Costs of an ATO objection, review or appeal
Interest charged by the ATO (GIC/SIC)
never_deductible: Tax shortfall penalties (s 26-5)

categories.label: P8
categories.name: Business - cost of goods sold
categories.rule: Opening stock + purchases - closing stock. Stock must be valued at cost, market selling value or replacement value, chosen per item each year.

categories.label: P-NONDED
categories.name: Entertainment (non-deductible)
categories.rule: Entertainment expenses are NOT deductible unless an exception in Subdiv 32-B applies, or the cost is subject to FBT.
never_deductible: Business lunches and dinners with clients
Tickets to sporting or cultural events
Golf days and corporate boxes
exceptions: Seminars of at least 4 hours where entertainment is incidental
Food provided to an employee that is subject to FBT
categories.risk_note: This is the most commonly misclassified business expense. Coding a client dinner to 'Meals' or 'Marketing' does not make it deductible.
categories.classification_trap: In Australia a great many pubs are licensed as Hotels, so a merchant name containing 'Hotel' is at least as likely to be a Friday lunch as it is accommodation. Where the description carries a meal or drinks signal, Div 32 entertainment is the safer reading and the deduction is denied. Treating it as D2 travel accommodation silently converts a non-deductible expense into a deductible one, which is the error direction that draws review.

categories.label: P-NONDED
categories.name: Fines and penalties (non-deductible)
categories.rule: Penalties or fines imposed by an Australian or foreign government body are never deductible.
